scenesAudited.scene3: L365-L599 (holly ambush, doe read, Millhaven overlook)

audits.notes: F13 demonstrative captions (6) and F12 non-action beats (6) are chapter-wide habits, not one-offs. F11 "It was in X. It was in Y." recurs across scenes; the cabbage-field instance is kept as sameness-is-content, the doe instance is killed as habit. Zero kills for F1, F2, F5, F8, F9, F10, with reasons in the scratchpad. Adversarial self-check: kills > 10; F7 found (L297); F11/F12/F13 checked per scene.

findings.text: Windrunner listened differently. Her attention never went to the door
findings.issue: Thesis-opening paragraph: "Windrunner listened differently." states the paragraph's claim, then the rest of the paragraph supplies the evidence (attention on the mouth, hunter simile). The evidence carries the point without the topic sentence.
findings.suggestedFix: Windrunner's attention never went to the door

findings.text: Nobody filled it.
findings.issue: Non-action beat, paragraph-final. The ward-stone humming "into the gap she'd left" already shows the silence. This is the second non-action beat in scene 1, after "The Ranger-General didn't move."

findings.text: Windrunner's voice didn't rise. It hadn't risen once.
findings.issue: Two stacked non-action beats ("didn't rise", "hadn't risen") that report an absence as a reaction. This is the third non-action beat in scene 1. Nothing had set up a shout here.
findings.suggestedFix: Windrunner said it at the same pitch as everything else.

findings.text: Windrunner said nothing, her face turned down the passage toward the guardroom.
findings.issue: "said nothing" is the fourth non-action reaction beat in scene 1. The positive half of the sentence (her face turned down the passage) already carries the silence that Jaina then reads.
findings.suggestedFix: Windrunner's face had turned down the passage toward the guardroom.

findings.text: That was all she said.
findings.issue: Caption-only demonstrative. It points back at Neral's "My lady." and labels it as complete. No new fact.

findings.text: So that was what the stones were to Windrunner: a gate, and a horse's manners at the gate.
findings.issue: Demonstrative caption. It labels the beat just shown (riders pass between the stones, horses sidestep, no ranger touches her reins). The next two sentences carry the real point (she promised proof at a stone and Windrunner rode past it). The cut also removes one narration colon from a chapter that is over its colon cap.
findings.pointsAt: the ride between the outer stones

findings.text: Lyriel said nothing.
findings.issue: Non-action beat that reports an absence the reader had no reason to expect. Lyriel has not spoken yet in the chapter, and the hand on the reins is the event. The scene's strongest non-action beat is "Windrunner didn't turn her head."
findings.suggestedFix: It was Lyriel.

findings.text: She held the reins a moment in the starlight, then let go and dropped back to Jaina's knee.
findings.issue: Temporal padding "a moment". Deletion test: "She held the reins in the starlight, then let go..." The beat still lands.
findings.deletionTest: She held the reins in the starlight, then let go and dropped back to Jaina's knee.
findings.suggestedFix: She held the reins in the starlight, then let go and dropped back to Jaina's knee.

findings.text: It was everywhere, and you couldn't ride to everywhere. You couldn't take everywhere apart on a bench.
findings.issue: Anaphoric run: "You couldn't... You couldn't" opens two consecutive sentences for drumbeat weight. A merged sentence loses nothing. This is the first run in scene 2. It is killed because the repeated frame carries no meaning a merge would lose.
findings.suggestedFix: It was everywhere, and you couldn't ride to everywhere, or take it apart on a bench.

findings.text: After the Pass, with its white-blue lamps and its stone, all of it seemed rumpled, a bed somebody had left in a hurry.
findings.issue: Hedge "seemed" softens a committed image. Deletion/substitution test: "all of it lay rumpled" is more direct, and the bed image carries the comparison.
findings.deletionTest: ...all of it lay rumpled, a bed somebody had left in a hurry.
findings.suggestedFix: After the Pass, with its white-blue lamps and its stone, all of it lay rumpled, a bed somebody had left in a hurry.

findings.text: hanging off the saddle a moment with her cheek against the mare's warm wet neck until the ground stopped tilting
findings.issue: Temporal padding "a moment". The "until the ground stopped tilting" clause already gives the duration.
findings.deletionTest: Jaina got down, hanging off the saddle with her cheek against the mare's warm wet neck until the ground stopped tilting.
findings.suggestedFix: hanging off the saddle with her cheek against the mare's warm wet neck until the ground stopped tilting

findings.text: That was a test for a bench and a lamp and a quiet room, and she had a horse to get onto.
findings.issue: Fact-bearing demonstrative caption. "That was a test for..." labels the unanswered question ("what a little did"). The fact that answering it needs a bench, a lamp and a quiet room stays, and the caption frame goes.
findings.suggestedFix: Finding out wanted a bench and a lamp and a quiet room, and she had a horse to get onto.

findings.text: And under all that, small and warm and entirely unasked for: someone had kept up.
findings.issue: Closure addiction. The sentence names the feeling ("small and warm and entirely unasked for") instead of leaving the recognition bare. It also edges past the plan's lock (constraints: "No trust and no warmth between Jaina and Sylvanas"; factsNotEarned: "Anything warmer than a grim, working alignment"). The recognition itself ("someone had kept up") and the filing gesture in the next sentence do the work.
findings.couldEndEarlierAt: someone had kept up. Jaina put that where useful things went and left it there.
findings.suggestedFix: And under all that: someone had kept up.

findings.text: She had no attention for the staff or for Jaina.
findings.issue: Over-translation. The paragraph already shows where Windrunner's attention is (head turned to the bend, hand on the fletching, the mare's ears pricked hard at the holly). The closing sentence restates it negatively.
findings.restates: Windrunner's head turned toward the bend, bow in hand, mare's ears on the holly

findings.text: and her hind legs kicking slowly at the air. Then they stopped.
findings.issue: Anaphoric run across a paragraph break: "Then they stopped." / "Then it was quiet." The two consecutive sentences open on the same "Then" frame for weight. Folding the first into the preceding clause keeps both facts.
findings.suggestedFix: and her hind legs kicking slowly at the air until they stopped.

findings.text: couldn't for the moment remember how she'd got there
findings.issue: Temporal padding "for the moment". Deletion test: "couldn't remember how she'd got there" lands the same, and the next sentences show that her disorientation passes.
findings.deletionTest: Jaina sat in the middle of the road on a horse blowing hard under her and couldn't remember how she'd got there.
findings.suggestedFix: couldn't remember how she'd got there

findings.text: So this was being put.
findings.issue: Demonstrative caption ("this was") that labels the callback the italics already made (*Off the road.* / *You don't step off the road unless I put you off it.*). No new fact.

findings.text: It was in the blood, thick and slow under the hide. It was in the meat too, deeper than the blood.
findings.issue: Anaphoric run "It was... It was..." immediately after "It was there at once". Three consecutive "It was" openers. This is the chapter's third use of the "It was in X. It was in Y." drumbeat (after the culvert and the cabbage field). Here it is a habit, not content.
findings.suggestedFix: The blood was thick and slow with it, and the meat deeper still.

findings.text: Light. That was the interesting part. Part of her sat up at it
findings.issue: Caption-only demonstrative. "That was the interesting part." ranks the previous paragraph's finding. The hound image that follows shows her interest without the label.
findings.pointsAt: the residue having grown through the doe while alive
findings.suggestedFix: Light. Part of her sat up at it

findings.text: She told it to wait, firmly, the way she'd have told a first-year.
findings.issue: Fenced manner adverb ", firmly," slowing a small act, followed by a "the way..." gloss that already says the same thing. The gloss carries her tutor-voice, so it stays. The adverb fails the deletion test.
findings.gloss: the way she'd have told a first-year
findings.suggestedFix: She told it to wait, the way she'd have told a first-year.

findings.text: It was the hour for supper. It was cold enough for a fire at noon.
findings.issue: Anaphoric run "It was... It was..." stating two premises with a drumbeat. Merging the two keeps both premises.
findings.suggestedFix: It was the hour for supper, and cold enough for a fire at noon.

findings.text: She didn't turn to Windrunner. She didn't need to.
findings.issue: Non-action beat pair in paragraph-final position ("She didn't turn... She didn't need to."), which is also an anaphoric "She didn't" run. The italic callback (*Most of them cross within a mile of the crossroads.*) already lands the recognition. The "didn't need to" closer is a stock model cadence.

findings.text: Nobody said anything. Jaina waited for a dog.
findings.issue: Non-action beat opening the paragraph. The paragraph goes on to build the silence positively (waiting for a dog, the race, the leather, the bit). "Nobody said anything" narrates an absence no one had set up.
findings.suggestedFix: Jaina waited for a dog.

findings.text: They could wait for morning. That was the sensible thing.
findings.issue: Fact-bearing demonstrative caption. "That was the sensible thing." labels the option just named. The judgment stays because the paragraph's closing question turns on "sensible", so the noun becomes the subject.
findings.suggestedFix: The sensible thing was to wait for morning.

findings.text: She wanted to go down. She wanted, very badly, not to. She wanted somebody else to choose, and she was angry with herself for wanting that.
findings.issue: Anaphoric triad "She wanted... She wanted... She wanted..." used for drumbeat weight, ending on an emotion-label tail ("angry with herself for wanting that") that the next paragraph repeats ("she hated that rather more"). Merging keeps the contradiction and drops the duplicated self-reproach.
findings.suggestedFix: She wanted to go down, and very badly not to, and under both she wanted somebody else to choose.

findings.text: She held the staff tight in her numb hand, the crystal humming, as the mare walked on down toward Millhaven.
findings.issue: Dying-fall coda at chapter end. It has a held object (the staff), a carry-on exit ("walked on down toward Millhaven") and nothing changes. The chapter has a stronger last beat one paragraph earlier, the unanswered question "Was there anyone? One person, anywhere in all those houses?"
findings.couldEndAt: Was there anyone? One person, anywhere in all those houses?

povRegister.registerSummary: Kirin Tor apprentice and leyline scholar, an admiral's daughter. She thinks in bench-and-lamp lab terms (first-years, jars, field-book) and in sea and ship images (hold, amidships, rigging, gulls), swears by the Light, and uses precise craft vocabulary (lattice, resonance, residue, pulse, lag). Proud, sleep-starved, quick to condescend to soldiers and quicker to flay herself for it. Wry self-mockery in free indirect thought. She would NOT think in detached aphorisms about soldier psychology, address an imagined reader as generic "you", or caption her own images with one-word verdicts.

audits.structuralHabit: Generic second-person "you" in narration similes (L287, L475; L193 kept as the one in-idiom use).

findings.text: A soldier wanted ground to stand on before she wanted a reason to stand there.
findings.issue: Polished chiastic aphorism ("ground to stand on / reason to stand there"). Jaina's condescension toward soldiers is plot and is kept, but this sentence is shaped like an epigraph rather than a muttered thought. The fix keeps the prejudice in her own concrete idiom.
findings.povMismatch: Too polished and symmetrical for a tired prisoner hauling her mind from argument to facts. It reads written, not thought.
findings.suggestedFix: A soldier would want somewhere to point a horse.

findings.text: a crate lashed down amidships. Cargo.
findings.issue: Verdict-tag fragment. "Cargo." labels the crate image that precedes it, so it captions the metaphor rather than adding a thought.
findings.povMismatch: Restates her own simile as a one-word verdict.
findings.suggestedFix: a crate lashed down amidships.

findings.text: the way you'd explain tides to a child who had never seen the sea
findings.issue: Generic "you" in third-person narration (the narrator addressing an imagined reader). The tides image is hers (admiral's daughter) and stays. Only the address changes.
findings.povMismatch: Generic-you address. The chapter keeps one generic you in her idiom ("you couldn't ride to everywhere"). This is a further one.
findings.suggestedFix: the way she'd have explained tides to a child who had never seen the sea

findings.text: Deer ran from horses. Every child in Lordaeron knew that much.
findings.issue: Generalizing construction ("Every child in Lordaeron knew") that zooms out to a population claim. "Deer ran from horses." is the in-moment operative fact, and Windrunner restates it in dialogue later ("Deer don't run at horses").
findings.povMismatch: Typifying a population mid-charge, when she has no time for it.
findings.suggestedFix: Deer ran from horses.

findings.text: hot the way the middle of a dung heap is hot when you push a spade into it on a frosty morning
findings.issue: Generic "you" inside a simile in third-person narration. The image stays. The address to an imagined reader goes.
findings.suggestedFix: hot the way the middle of a dung heap is hot when a spade goes into it on a frosty morning

repeatStandIns: cost/costs (L259, L263) - anchored by guard ring, kept
audits.killRateNote: Keep rate exceeds the guide's 25% heuristic. Each keep was re-challenged under the Step 4 anti-rationalization check. The chapter's analytical lines are almost all followed or preceded by named field signs (coin taste, late drag, frost fern, ruts full of rain, organ order). The one status-note line with no work left to do (L263) is killed.

findings.text: Jaina had what she'd knelt down for.
findings.issue: Planner shorthand / status note. It summarizes the culvert read from above ("had what she came for") and would fit unchanged on a beat card. The read itself was shown in full two paragraphs earlier, and "Fine. Let her count her costs." already lands the defiance.
findings.failedQuestion: What does this cash out to?
findings.missingPayload: the actual finding (it left the line, into clay, water, roots). It is already on the page, so the line is pure status summary

audits.cleanReason: 8 candidates audited across both "short version" setups (L23 reply L25-27; L269 "Short." reply L277) and every question-to-answer exchange where Windrunner asks for usable output (L61/L73 "Which stones/Where", L299-301 source-or-sink, L469 "Tell me what's in her", L523 "How long?", L529 "Is it in my horses?", L537 "Where's it strongest?"). The two fake simplifications in the chapter are the dramatized character flaw the plan requires (arcPosition: "Because she assumes soldiers need the short version, she talks smaller than she really thinks"). The text punctures both in-scene (L35 self-critique; Windrunner's correction at L279-283 and Jaina's condemnation at L287), and each is followed by a reply with usable target and trigger. Every reply Windrunner acts on names a usable target, a visible threshold, or a direction she can order a ride on.

summary.verdictReason: fail: 1 MODERATE kill (F7 warmth label at L297 that edges past the plan's no-warmth lock) plus 31 MILD kills (threshold 3). Dominant habits: F13 demonstrative captions, F12 non-action beats, F11 "It was / She wanted" anaphora, generic-you narration (A7). Structural rhythm concerns: sentence_length_cv, one_sentence_paragraph_pct, long_sentence_pct, opener_entropy, mattr outside style-guide range. Structural texture deficit: texture below_target (score 75.1; participial 6.2% vs 12%, compound 13.7% vs 10%, em-dash 1.5% vs 4%), 12 telegram runs, 20 texture deserts.
